provinces.name: Tir Aoda
provinces.notes: Kilaoda, St. Aoda's, the great cloister.

settlements.name: Wealdburh
settlements.notes: Royal seat of Northwold, where the Old Way ends: the king's long timber hall stands on an older mound inside a double burh bank. Moor shepherds and charcoal-burners bring their quarrels to its moot. The king's reeve keeps a tally-stick for every hide of the realm.

settlements.name: Kelpwick
settlements.notes: Fishing and wrack-gathering village on the windy north-west strand. Its boats go out in pairs since a feud over a drowned net-mender ended in two funerals.

settlements.name: Cocklewick
settlements.notes: Cockle-pickers and salt-boilers at the head of a shallow bay; the tide goes out a full league and the children race it back.

settlements.name: Curlewham
settlements.notes: A clutch of turf-roofed steadings in a moorland hollow. The shepherds read weather from the curlews and pay their dues to Wealdburh in fleeces.

settlements.name: Saltburh
settlements.notes: Northwold's salt port: brine pans steam below the cliff-top burh, and the king's salt-reeve taxes every cartload. Its burh bank has been rebuilt twice in living memory, both times after the raiders had gone home.

settlements.name: Selhythe
settlements.notes: St. Cuthric's lanternhouse on a seal-haunted islet off Saltburh, reached at low water by a causeway of stepping stones. The brothers copy holy books for half the kings of Albrenn and keep a beacon lit on the cliff for fishermen.

settlements.name: Holmwick
settlements.notes: Ferry and eel-weirs at the mouth of the Holm. The ferryman charges strangers double and kings nothing.

settlements.name: Rookburh
settlements.notes: A cliff-top burh of earth and timber guarding Northwold's northern landings, garrisoned by the king's thegns in turns. Its rookery is older than its walls, and the garrison counts the birds as lookouts.

settlements.name: Thelwick
settlements.notes: Royal seat of Merewood at the head of navigation on the Mere: barges from the coast unload at a plank wharf below the king's hall. The queen-dowager runs the wharf-tolls and, some say, the kingdom.

settlements.name: Leofham
settlements.notes: relicHolder:boneHarp. A prosperous market town on the Old Way, home to a skald family who have kept the Harp of Hollow Bone for five generations and play it only at royal funerals. Every ambitious lord in Albrenn has tried to buy it.

settlements.name: Frithburh
settlements.notes: A burh where the Old Way squeezes between the Merewood crags; its gate closes the road north. Travellers swear the king's peace at the gate and pay a penny for the privilege.

settlements.name: Coltham
settlements.notes: Horse-breeders on the eastern meadows of Merewood. The king's riders get their mounts here, and every colt is promised to someone before it is foaled.

settlements.name: Holtham
settlements.notes: Woodcutters and swineherds in the western holts. They sell oak to the Thelwick wharves and acorn-fattened pork to anyone.

settlements.name: Marshcester
settlements.notes: An old earthwork burh on a fen island, raised above the reeds on a causeway of oak piles. Its reeve grows rich on eel-rents and on the tolls of the Old Way.

settlements.name: Tollham
settlements.notes: Where the Old Way and the West Way meet: a toll-bar, two alehouses and a smithy that shoes every horse going south. The toll-reeve is the most hated man in Fenholt and knows it.

settlements.name: Mireham
settlements.notes: Reed-cutters and wildfowlers on the dry edge of the fen. They thatch half the roofs of Merewood.

settlements.name: Sedgeford
settlements.notes: A forest town at the sedge-fringed ford by the Hollow Mere, where Hollowmere's ealdorman holds court. He owes service to Merewood but keeps his own counsel, and his foresters know every path in the western woods.

settlements.name: Wrenwick
settlements.notes: St. Ambrel's lanternhouse on a wind-bent headland facing the Cael Sound. Its brothers ransom captives taken by Cael raiders and keep the Sound's oldest book of tides.

settlements.name: Brinewick
settlements.notes: Salt-boilers and herring-smokers on Hollowmere's west strand. Cael traders beach their boats here in summer, and not always to trade.

settlements.name: Brackenham
settlements.notes: A few crofts above a stony cove at the foot of the western hills; the only path in is by sea or over the bracken fells.

settlements.name: Honeyford
settlements.notes: Bee-keepers and mead-brewers in the green vale east of the hills. The village pays part of its tribute in wax candles for the lanternhouses.

settlements.name: Aldermouth
settlements.notes: Royal seat of Westmere on the Saffren estuary, ringed by an alder-stake palisade and a deep burh ditch. Its king keeps a fleet of knarrs and a long memory for slights.

settlements.name: Hawkburh
settlements.notes: A hill burh above the pass where the West Way crosses the Westmere crags. The king's falconers winter here, and the garrison eats well.

settlements.name: Otterwick
settlements.notes: A creek village under the oak woods of the north shore; boat-builders and trappers of otter and marten.

settlements.name: Gorsham
settlements.notes: Gorse-burners and goat-herds on the western headland. They light a fire on the cliff when Cael sails are seen, and expect to be paid for it.

settlements.name: Elderford
settlements.notes: A road village at the upper ford of the Saffren. The ford-keeper's daughters run the alehouse and hear every rumour on the West Way.

settlements.name: Chalkford
settlements.notes: Wool town of the chalk downs, where the Downs Track crosses a clear stream. Its wool-moot sets the price of a fleece from here to Gullhythe.

settlements.name: Keelhythe
settlements.notes: Shipwrights' town in a sheltered creek; its yards build knarrs for half of Albrenn. The master-wright's guild hates outsiders and loves their silver.

settlements.name: Wendleford
settlements.notes: River village where barges on the Wendle turn back at the shallows. Bargemen and drovers drink together and fight over who pays.

settlements.name: Kittiwick
settlements.notes: Fisher-crofts under the white cliffs of the Chalk Isle, loud with nesting kittiwakes. At low tide a reef shows, and the wreckers' tales start.

settlements.name: Combeham
settlements.notes: Cider orchards and a sheltered harbour at the mouth of the combe. Its reeve pays Westmere in cider barrels, and it is said Westmere pays the Cael in the same coin.

settlements.name: Bellham
settlements.notes: St. Goda's lanternhouse at the edge of the south-western marshes. Its bronze bell, cast by a smith from over the sea, is the largest in Albrenn and can be heard across the bay on a still day.

settlements.name: Sloeford
settlements.notes: Hedge-bound fields and blackthorn lanes at the head of the vale. Its sloe-wine is sour, strong and exported by the barrel.

settlements.name: Gyrwick
settlements.notes: Royal seat of Eastfen on a gravel spit between fen and sea; the king's hall is built of ship-timbers. The fen-folk say no army has ever found the causeway twice.

settlements.name: Merewick
settlements.notes: Trading wic at the mouth of the Mere, where sea-going ships meet the river barges from Thelwick. Corvani wine-merchants keep a quarter here, and Merewood and Eastfen quarrel over its tolls.

settlements.name: Larkham
settlements.notes: Barley fields and a beach landing on the open coast north of the Mere. Raiders know it well; so do its archers.

settlements.name: Eelhythe
settlements.notes: Fen landing at the head of a reedy bay; eel-traps, punts and wildfowl. Its people pay their rent in eels, counted by the stick of twenty-five.

settlements.name: Gullhythe
settlements.notes: Seawold's great harbour beside the Wendle's mouth, where a stone tower of the old empire, now the lanternhouse's beacon, lights the channel. Merchants from every coast winter here, and the harbour-reeve's ledgers are the best intelligence in Albrenn.

settlements.name: Swanhythe
settlements.notes: St. Wenna's lanternhouse on a wooded headland above a quiet lagoon where swans winter. The abbess is a king's widow and still behaves like one.

settlements.name: Tarwick
settlements.notes: Pitch-boilers and net-makers on the south shore; their tar caulks the hulls of Gullhythe. The smoke can be seen from the sea a day off.

settlements.name: Yewham
settlements.notes: Bowyers in the old yew-woods north of Gullhythe; their staves sell well to the Hvarn.

settlements.name: Dun Brac
settlements.notes: Royal seat of Brac: a stone-walled dun on a sea-rock at the mouth of a deep loch, reached by one causeway. The kings of Brac have been crowned on its threshold stone for longer than anyone remembers.

settlements.name: Dun Rua
settlements.notes: The red fort on the northern headland of Brac, built of red sandstone. Its warband watches the Whale-Road and takes a share of anything wrecked below.

settlements.name: Ballycorr
settlements.notes: Herons and fishing coracles on the green east shore under the mountains. The village owes its kings three boats and their crews each summer.

settlements.name: Liscorra
settlements.notes: A ring-fort village on the western machair facing the Inishvar isles. Cattle-raids between Liscorra and the islanders are an old sport.

settlements.name: Ballyhessa
settlements.notes: Brac's southern harbour, a creek village of fishermen and boat-hirers who ferry folk across to Morra.

settlements.name: Inishvar
settlements.notes: Island town of the outer isles, built of drystone and turf, where the islanders gather for law-days. Its chief is a seal-hunter who owes Brac service and seldom pays.

settlements.name: Inisheala
settlements.notes: Swan isle: a handful of crofts among the northern marshes, where whooper swans come in winter.

settlements.name: Inishmael
settlements.notes: St. Maelis's lanternhouse on the farthest isle: beehive cells, a stone chapel and a boat that rarely leaves. The monks keep bees and illuminate holy books prized as far as Saraleon.

settlements.name: Kilmorra
settlements.notes: Royal seat of Ulmorra at the head of a sea loch, grown around an old church and a king's rath. The kings of Ulmorra keep a cattle-tally bigger than any treasury.

settlements.name: Kilfennic
settlements.notes: St. Fennic's lanternhouse on a green islet in the northern firth, famous for its scholars and its herb garden. Pilgrims come by boat at the saint's feast.

settlements.name: Lisgorm
settlements.notes: A blue-slate ring-fort and its village on the western sea-meadows. Its chief is an old raider who still sails when the harvest is in.

settlements.name: Glenbran
settlements.notes: Raven glen: a fishing village at the foot of the eastern mountains, looking across the Sound to Albrenn.

settlements.name: Ballacree
settlements.notes: Morra's market harbour on the Cael Sound, where Albric traders buy hides, wool and hounds. Its fair at harvest draws half the island and ends, by custom, in a stick-and-ball game that kills someone most years.

settlements.name: Glencorrin
settlements.notes: St. Corrin's lanternhouse in a quiet glen above the southern shore. Its abbot is the king of Ulmorra's brother, and his advice is not always holy.

settlements.name: Ballyardan
settlements.notes: Village on the eastern shore of Lough Ardan; fishermen, reed-cutters and a crannog on the lake where the chief keeps his treasure.

settlements.name: Dunlirr
settlements.notes: A small dun at the bog crossing of the upper Lirr. Bog-iron smelters work here, and the paths across the bog are known only to locals.

settlements.name: Lisdara
settlements.notes: Royal seat of Desmor: an oak-palisaded rath at the head of a narrow southern inlet, under the mountains. Its kings are famous for hospitality and for murdering guests who abuse it.

settlements.name: Kilorla
settlements.notes: St. Orla's lanternhouse on a southern headland, a nunnery of healers whose infirmary takes in anyone, raider or king.

settlements.name: Ballyrean
settlements.notes: Bog-cutters and salt-marsh fishers on the eastern shore; famous for smoked salmon and bad roads.

settlements.name: Glencarrow
settlements.notes: Cattle country in the northern glen; the herds of Desmor's kings summer on its pastures, and raiders from Ulmorra know it.

settlements.name: Kilaoda
settlements.notes: relicHolder:grayComb. St. Aoda's, the great cloister of the west and the richest lanternhouse in the Cael Isles; its treasury is a windowless stone house beside the oratory. The reliquary holds the Gray Queen's Comb, kept by a sisterhood of healers. Kings of all three Cael realms lie in its yard.

settlements.name: Ballyvreen
settlements.notes: Fishing village on Tir Aoda's northern strand; its boats carry pilgrims to Kilaoda and gossip to everyone.

settlements.name: Glenvarra
settlements.notes: Shielings in the boggy glen of the Lirr, where Kilaoda grazes its cattle and cuts its turf.

sites.name: Whale-Stack
sites.notes: A sheer sea-stack north of Brac, white with gannets. Hidden in an eyrie ledge, the islanders say, lies the Whalebone War-Horn; the climb needs a calm weather window (Vigor/Wildcraft).

sites.name: the Bellowing Cave
sites.notes: A sea-cave on Brac's west coast that booms like a bull at half-tide. Seal-hunters shelter in it; outlaws have been known to.

sites.name: Goda's Hole
sites.notes: The cliff cave where St. Goda is said to have lived as a hermit. Pilgrims leave rags on the thorn at its mouth; the tide floods the inner chamber.

sites.name: the Copper Hollow
sites.notes: An old copper working in the Carrowmor mountains, long abandoned; the shafts are flooded and the props are rotten.

sites.name: Wetherdown Barrow
sites.notes: A long barrow on the chalk downs, older than the Albric kings. The shepherds will not graze it and a family of hereditary wardens claims the right to bury their dead there.

sites.name: Carn Fiach
sites.notes: The raven cairn: a great stone burial-cairn on a Glenmorra ridge, said to hold a forgotten king and his war-gear.

sites.name: Ashenhall
sites.notes: The burned hall of a Northwold thegn whose house was wiped out in a feud a generation ago. Charred posts and a fallen roof; outlaws use it in winter.

sites.name: the Burnt Rath
sites.notes: A ring-fort and hall burned in a cattle-raid. Squatters live in the outbuildings and swear the chief's hoard was never found.

sites.name: Fenshoal Wreck
sites.notes: A Corvani merchantman stranded on the Eastfen shoals in a winter gale; its ribs show at low spring tides. Salvage needs the right tide and a local who knows the channels.

sites.name: Red Heron Wreck
sites.notes: A raider ship broken on the reef of a lonely islet west of Tir Aoda; the islanders say her chest went down with her.

sites.name: the Westwatch
sites.notes: A ruined signal tower of the old empire on the cliffs of Westmere, overlooking the Cael Sound. A hermit lives in its stump and keeps watch for a fee.

sites.name: Nine Oaks
sites.notes: A ring of ancient oaks deep in the Merewood forest, where the old gods were worshipped before the Lantern came. Some of the woodcutters still leave offerings there, and the priests pretend not to know.
